key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current affect molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability in distinct ways.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide parameter selection for Invar welds used in aerospace composite tooling.
method: High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior
Parameter study of laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: Within the reported ranges, increasing laser power (5–6 kW) deepened penetration and promoted arc deflection, increasing speed (0.5–0.8 m/min) narrowed and shallowed the weld, and increasing current (150–170 A) widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends over limited parameter ranges, but provides no quantitative simulation–experiment agreement or defect-based process window.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
